# SD GIS Hub

A local Django app that keeps a census of the public GIS data South Dakota governments publish, archives the datasets worth keeping (the latest data from each harvest), and lets you search, map and download all of it, including a fuzzy search across every owner and taxpayer name in the archive.

Run the commands below from the repository root.

## Setup

Requirements:

- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 22
- Postgres 17 with PostGIS on port 5432 ([Postgres.app](https://postgresapp.com/) includes it)
- Redis (`brew install redis && brew services start redis`)

```sh
just setup                            # uv sync, npm ci + Tailwind build, pre-commit hooks
createdb sd_gis_hub
just manage migrate
just manage load_jurisdictions        # 789 places with boundaries, from sdplaces (see Layout)
just manage seed                      # publishers, sources and watched datasets from seeds/sources.toml
just manage import_beacon_clients     # South Dakota's Beacon apps, from seeds/beacon-clients.html
just manage createsuperuser           # for /admin/
```

Database settings come from the usual `PG*` environment variables. The default database is `sd_gis_hub` on `localhost`.

The FEC record sets read `FEC_API_KEY`, a free [api.data.gov key](https://api.open.fec.gov/developers/). Without one they use the FEC's shared `DEMO_KEY`, which allows only a few requests an hour.

## Running it

```sh
just serve                     # http://localhost:8000
just worker                    # runs crawls and harvests
just beat                      # starts scheduled crawls and harvests
```

Without a worker, the buttons in the app queue jobs that wait on the Jobs page. Everything also runs from the command line without Celery:

```sh
just crawl                     # crawl every active source (or: just crawl minnehaha sddot)
just harvest                   # harvest every watched dataset (or: just harvest 641 --force)
just scrape <slug>             # run a record set's source (--force past the drop guard)
just documents <slug>          # fetch, read, categorize and extract its documents (--steps, --limit, --model)
just manage retry_documents    # send failed documents back to the step they failed at (--recordset, --dry-run)
just manage compare_source <slug>  # what a run would change, compared with the stored records
just manage adopt_legacy <slug>    # before a source's first run: give imported records its keys (--dry-run)
just manage import_prl_snapshots <slug>  # an earlier system's snapshots of items it no longer kept, as dropped records
just manage build_readme       # refresh the sources table above
just status                    # what's running, stalled, failed or overdue; partial downloads; disk; backups
```

**Stopping and starting again.** Anything can be stopped at any point (a closed lid, a crash) and picks up where it was:
- A harvest saves each downloaded batch to `media/staging/` as it arrives. A stopped harvest leaves them there, and the next run reuses them and fetches only the rest. They're removed once the harvest is stored.
- A job whose worker stopped partway is marked *stalled* on the scheduler's next tick, and the crawl or harvest it left open is closed, so it runs again when due.
- Schedules catch up once: after days asleep, an overdue crawl or harvest runs one time, not once per missed day.
- On macOS, a failed job shows a notification: the first failure after a success, and again at three in a row (`SD_NOTIFY=0` turns them off).

## What's in the app

| Page | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Name search** `/search/` | Fuzzy search over owner, taxpayer and other name fields in harvested datasets, grouped by name |
| **Datasets** `/datasets/` | The census: search names, descriptions and fields; filter by place, topic, source, status. |
| Dataset page | **Overview** (fields, count history, schema changes) · **Map** (vector tiles from the archive, or a live sample from the source) · **Table** (sort and filter every record) · **Changes** (each harvest's counts of added, changed and removed records) · **Download** (GeoParquet, GeoJSON, CSV). **Watch** a dataset to harvest it on a schedule |
| Record page | One record's attributes and location, as of the latest harvest |
| **Places** `/places/` | Every county, city, town and tribal area: what it publishes, by topic, and what's missing |
| **Coverage** `/coverage/` | Counties × topics |
| **Sources** `/sources/` | Each server: crawl history, services that errored, a **Crawl now** button |
| **Changes** `/changes/` | New and removed datasets, and harvests that found changes |
| **Jobs** `/jobs/` | Every crawl and harvest, live |
| **Admin** `/admin/` | Edit sources, folder-to-place mappings, topics and their rules, name fields, schedules |
| **API** `/api/v1/docs` | Datasets, features (with `bbox`), places, name search |

## How it works

**Census.**
- A crawl reads a source's services directory and records every queryable layer and table: fields, counts, paging support and description.
- Each crawl also stores an observation, so feature counts and schemas have a history.
- Datasets are marked removed only when a crawl reads every service on the server. A stopped service or a timeout never looks like a deletion.
- Shared servers map folders or the start of service names to places. For example, 1stdistrict's `Lawrence/` folder belongs to Lawrence County, and District III's `BON_HOMME1_FSA_2021` service to Bon Homme County.
- Each field's code labels are kept with the dataset (a `STATUS` of `3` means "Under construction"), along with the layer's last edit date when the server reports one.
- Rules on layer and field names assign topics and suggest name fields. Anything set by hand in the admin wins over the rules.
- Copies are left out: when a layer is published in several services, only the original is kept. A copy has the same place, geometry and count, and its fields match the original's or nearly all appear in it (at least 10 in common). The original is the watched or harvested one, else the one with the most fields, on a main service, a FeatureServer, the oldest. Copies already recorded are deleted, and the crawl log reports how many were skipped.
- Search indexes that only repeat other layers' text (First District's `AutoComplete` tables) are skipped entirely.

**Harvest.**
- A watched dataset is downloaded in object ID ranges, which works whether or not the server supports pagination. Batches the server truncates are split in half and retried.
- The download is checked against the server's count, for duplicate IDs, and against a sudden drop (`max_drop`, 10% by default; use force to override).
- It's then compared with the archive:
  - unchanged records are left alone
  - a changed record is overwritten
  - a record missing from the source is kept and marked *dropped*, with when it was first found gone; it's unmarked if it comes back
- Only the latest version of each record is kept: no earlier versions. Maps, tables, downloads, counts and name search show current records; a dropped record keeps its page, which says when it went, and each harvest's page lists the records it dropped.
- Each harvest that changes something also rewrites the dataset's GeoParquet file (`media/exports/<dataset>/latest.parquet`).
- Hosted layers report when their data last changed. If that date and the count both match the last full harvest, the harvest is recorded as skipped instead of downloading again, with a full download at least weekly regardless. Most ArcGIS Server layers don't report the date, so they're always downloaded.
- The archive stores raw codes. The table and record pages show each code's label next to it, and CSV downloads add a `FIELD_label` column.
- The download is saved batch by batch (see "Stopping and starting again"); storing it commits or rolls back as one unit.

**Records.**
- Each record set's code is in `records/sources/<name>/`: `source.py` (its `Source`: how to fetch the items, each with the source's own key, its fields, its files' URLs and the places it's in; for documents, the categories, rules and Pydantic extraction schemas that read them; the named parties for mentions), `parse.py` (pure parsing, which raises rather than skip a row it can't read), `schema.py`, and `tests/` with fixtures cut from the real pages and a recording of the live site.
- Each run fetches through a store of its own (`media/raw/<slug>/`, with a manifest of every response). Sources that make many requests store each response under the month, so a stopped run reuses what it already fetched.
- Hand corrections to what a source publishes (a row linked to the wrong file) go in its `fixes.toml` (`records.fixes`): each names the row, the value published and the corrected one, and why. It's applied only while the source still publishes the value it corrects, and recorded on the record (`corrections`).
- Places: each record links to the jurisdictions it's in or about (several for a registration spanning counties), by the GEOID sdplaces gives for the place in force on the record's date.
- Records imported from an earlier system are checked against a source with `compare_source` (the source's `from_legacy` puts the old data in its shape) and given its keys with `adopt_legacy`, which keeps when each was first seen and merges imported duplicates of one item.
- A run stores the items the same way a harvest stores features: unchanged ones are left alone, changed ones overwritten (keeping when each was first seen), and after a complete run, ones gone from the source kept and marked dropped (`Record.objects.current()` and `.dropped()`). A complete run that finds far fewer items than are stored is refused (`max_drop`). A record's documents follow its list of files; a file it stops listing is kept and marked dropped.
- Documents go through steps, each one moving a document on or marking it failed with the error, without stopping the rest:
  - **fetch**: the file is stored once by its SHA-256 in `media/blobs/`, with every fetch logged in `media/manifest.jsonl`. A web page where a file was expected (an error page, a login form) isn't stored. The file type comes from the bytes, not the server's label.
  - **read**: form fields or the text layer, else OCR (`SD_OCR_ENGINE`, rapidocr by default), page by page and cached in `media/pages/`. Images are read as one-page PDFs.
  - **categorize**: the source's rule, else a model choosing among its categories. A category without a schema has nothing to extract, which finishes the document.
  - **extract**: the category's fields, each with the quote it came from, checked against the text (sdllm). Fields without a found quote are flagged. A new reading replaces unreviewed ones and never touches reviewed ones.
  - **review**: approving or correcting a reading finishes the document; rejecting it leaves it for a new reading.
- A record is complete when every document is finished. `just status` lists failed documents, readings waiting on review, and records stuck for a day with every document failed or waiting.

**Name search.**
- After each harvest, the dataset's name fields go into `search_nameentry`, normalized by the SQL function `gis_hub_normalize_name()` (uppercase, accents removed, punctuation stripped) and indexed with `pg_trgm`.
- The view `search_names` exposes those rows in a shared format, which other databases on the same server can publish too, so one search can cover them all.

## Adding a source

Paste any URL on the server into the box on the Sources page: the services directory, a folder, a layer, or just the host name. The hub finds the services directory, lists what it publishes and suggests which places its top-level folders and service names belong to (`BON_HOMME1_FSA_2021` → Bon Homme County). Check the suggestions, then **Add and crawl**.

[`seeds/sources.toml`](seeds/sources.toml) always matches the database: the app rewrites it after any change to a source, publisher or watched dataset, wherever the change was made (these pages, the admin, a crawl). `manage.py seed` loads it into a rebuilt database. You can also edit it by hand; run `seed` afterwards, before changing anything in the app, or the app will overwrite your edits. Beacon portals are left out, because `import_beacon_clients` rebuilds them. If one server hosts several governments, map its folders or service-name prefixes to place slugs (see the 1stdistrict entry). To watch datasets every time the database is rebuilt, add `[[watch]]` entries.

## Analysis

`harvest.frames.load_dataset()` loads a harvested dataset as a GeoDataFrame, from `just manage shell` or any script that sets up Django:

```python
from harvest.frames import load_dataset

parcels = load_dataset(641)  # the records as of the latest harvest
```

## Development

```sh
just test                        # tests use a throwaway Postgres database and a fake ArcGIS server
uv run pytest -m network         # one test against a live server
just check                       # every pre-commit hook
```

Layout:
- `../packages/sdgis/`: plain-Python ArcGIS and Beacon clients, with no Django imports
- `places/`: `Jurisdiction`, every place records are about, loaded from sdplaces with Census boundaries: the state, counties, cities and towns, census designated places, tribal areas, school districts and legislative districts. Former places stay, with the date they ended and what they became (Shannon County → Oglala Lakota County). Each has its GEOID, fully qualified GEOID (unique across kinds) and Open Civic Data ID.
- `entities/`: `Mention`, one name as a record gives it, typed with [Follow the Money](https://followthemoney.tech/) schemas (Person, Company, Organization, PublicBody, LegalEntity). An owner string with several people gives one mention each (`entities.mentions.from_text`, through sdnames), so each can be matched to a different entity. Every mention keeps its dataset, record key, field, role, the original string and a link to the primary source. `just manage load_legislator_gold <profiles folder>` loads legislators' session profiles with hand-checked identities (`entities/gold/legislators.csv`: each sdlegislature.gov session profile ID → the legislator's canonical ID), a gold set for scoring name matching.
- `records/`: public records by record set (lobbyist registrations, executive orders, filings): a `Record` per item at the source (its fields, keyed by the source's own key, as of the latest run), its `Document`s (files, stored once by SHA-256), and `Extraction`s (fields read from a document by a model, with the quote for each, and their review). Each `Run` of a source logs what it found and changed. A watched GIS layer is a record set too: its features are records with a geometry, and each harvest is a run. `just manage import_prl` imports an existing database of these.
- `census/`: sources, datasets, crawls, topics
- `harvest/`: downloading watched layers into their record sets (validation, staging, the drop guard), plus tiles, tables and exports. It has no tables of its own.
- `search/`: the name index
- `core/`: jobs and scheduling
- `config/`: settings, Celery, URLs and the API
- The `published` database schema holds the views that define what can be exported (`published.places`, `published.gis_datasets`). The `sd_export` role can read those views and nothing else; mentions aren't in it.
